html:
Ranjit Singh was the founder and first maharaja of the Sikh Empire in the Punjab, ruling from 1801 until his death in 1839. He was known as the Lion of Punjab.

He was the son of a chief of one of the Sikh misls, the bands of warriors that shared power in the Punjab after the decline of the Mughals and the raids of Ahmad Shah Durrani. He became chief as a boy. In 1799 he took Lahore, and in 1801 he was proclaimed maharaja.

He united the misls and conquered outward:

  • He took Amritsar, the Sikh holy city, and covered the upper storeys of its Harmandir Sahib in gilded copper, which gave it the name Golden Temple.
  • He won Multan from the Afghans in 1818 and Kashmir in 1819, and later Peshawar.
  • He built a modern army drilled by French and Italian officers who had served Napoleon.
  • He took the Koh-i-Noor diamond from the exiled Afghan king Shah Shuja.

His state reached from the Khyber Pass to the Sutlej, and from Ladakh to the borders of Sindh, and neighbours such as Bahawalpur lived in its shadow. He kept peace with the British East India Company by a treaty of 1809 that fixed the Sutlej as the border. He gave high posts to Hindus and Muslims, though his troops used Lahore's Badshahi Mosque as a stable and magazine. After his death his heirs fought each other, and the British annexed the Punjab in 1849 after two wars.
sum: Ranjit Singh was the founder and first maharaja of the Sikh Empire in the Punjab, ruling from 1801 until his death in 1839. He was known as the Lion of Punjab.
